headline: This law extends the Lifespan Respite Care Program through fiscal year 2024 and requires grant-receiving state agencies to report program data.
what_it_does: The law reauthorizes the Lifespan Respite Care Program, which funds state services for family caregivers of children and adults with special needs. It runs the program through fiscal year 2024. It also requires each state agency that receives a grant to report any data the Department of Health and Human Services asks for so the program can be monitored and evaluated.

who_it_affects.group: Family caregivers of children and adults with special needs
who_it_affects.how: The program that funds state respite care services for them is extended through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: State agencies that receive lifespan respite care grants
who_it_affects.how: They must report any data required by the Department of Health and Human Services for program monitoring and evaluation.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 5, 2021; the reauthorization covers funding through fiscal year 2024.
